html: Check the filter plan, not just the fitted cartridge: Breville's current BES870XL instruction book recommends replacing the supplied water filter about every two months, more often in hard-water areas. It also says to remove that filter when using filtered or bottled water; its purpose is to reduce scale buildup, not replace descaling. For a used machine, ask what water entered the tank, when the cartridge was changed and whether a solid descale prompt was completed. A new cartridge alone says little about prior water care. Checked October 20, 2026. [source]
note: Current BES870 North American book, page 22: roughly two-month filter replacement guidance, more often for hard water, and filter removal when using filtered or bottled water.

html: Check that an EC685 descale finishes: De'Longhi says the orange warning can keep flashing when the rinse has not registered. Its remedy completes a water-only stage and rinse, then returns the steam dial to off. For a used unit, verify the warning clears. Follow the manual for chemicals. Checked October 20, 2026. [source]
note: Manufacturer EC680/EC685 troubleshooting distinguishes a completed descaling rinse and dial-off state from an unregistered cycle with a still-flashing light.

html: Confirm the first-start kit and boiler fill: Rancilio North America's Silvia Classic setup guide lists a double-spout portafilter, single and double baskets, backflush disk, tablets, tamper and dosing spoon in its accessory kit. It also tells a new owner to check the two reservoir tubes, fill with filtered water, and run hot water through the wand so the boiler is saturated. For a used V6, missing water tubes or backflush gear change the handover and care budget; demonstrate hot-water flow before judging shot quality. The manufacturer guide is setup evidence, not a promise about every regional bundle or machine condition. Checked October 20, 2026. [source]
note: Rancilio North America Silvia Classic setup lists accessory-kit contents, reservoir-tube check and hot-water boiler-saturation step.

html: The BES878 screen has two different care jobs: the US instruction book calls its FLUSH prompt a tablet cleaning cycle, separate from DESCALE. Descaling proceeds through coffee, hot water and steam stages; the owner must turn the steam dial to the hot-water and steam positions when the LCD instructs. When inspecting a used Barista Pro, verify that the menu, dial and all three outlets respond and ask whether the full rinse followed descaling. A cleared FLUSH prompt alone does not establish water-path maintenance. This is manufacturer procedure and buyer guidance, not a claim that a particular machine was maintained. Checked October 20, 2026. [source]
note: US BES878 book identifies FLUSH as separate from DESCALE and describes three descale stages with manual hot-water and steam dial changes.

html: Use the K-Ultra's real zero after cleaning: 1Zpresso defines zero as the point where the handle begins to turn with resistance, not the tightest position of the dial. Its K-Ultra manual says to check whether the pointer reads 0 after reassembly and adjust the thumb nut if it does not; it also says not to wash or soak the grinder. If a used grinder's recipe numbers seem inexplicably different, check that gentle zero and the part order before blaming the burrs or copying someone else's setting. Do not force the ring closed to make a printed zero line up. Checked October 20, 2026. [source]
note: Exact K-Ultra manual defines resistance-based zero, dial-pointer calibration after reassembly and dry-cleaning precautions.
